A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NMMO research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Sections 7–8 of v1 correspond to Appendices A–B of v2; relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original optimization experiments on six real-world problems and ZDT3, including method comparisons, ablations, and measured runtimes.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Appendix A.4 adds original evaluations on four DTLZ configurations with four or five objectives.

M1.justification: The Nested, Joint, and BINOM acquisition functions, HVI reward, and lookahead GP approximation remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 clarifies acquisition-function labels and optimization domains already described in v1, without changing the procedures.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained six real-world problems and ZDT3, Appendix A.4 adds DTLZ1 with (d,K)=(11,4) and (7,5), DTLZ2 with (8,4), and DTLZ3 with (9,5). This substantially extends evaluated coverage from two or three objectives to four and five objectives across additional synthetic landscapes.

E2.justification: EHVI, JESMO, MESMO, and HVKG were already evaluated in v1 and remain in the corresponding comparisons. The added DTLZ experiments use existing EHVI and JESMO comparators; they introduce no new comparison method.

E3.justification: The stated setup retains five Sobol initialization points, 65 BO iterations, independent Matérn 5/2 ARD GPs, and hypervolume evaluation. Existing reference points and horizon settings are retained. The DTLZ extension introduces no separately stated change to the evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The dedicated lookahead-horizon studies, EHVI/MESMO/JESMO scalarization ablation, and runtime analysis are retained. Figure 6 adds DTLZ benchmark comparisons using several existing horizon settings, without a distinct new ablation or robustness analysis. Moving scalarization discussion into Appendix A.3 does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging experiments over 15 runs, show shaded uncertainty bands, and report runtime means and standard deviations across 65 iterations of one run. No new seed information, uncertainty definition, or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds substantial performance evidence for four higher-objective DTLZ configurations. Its final plotted means favor BINOM with H=2 on DTLZ1(11,4), but NMMO-Joint with H=2 on DTLZ3(9,5). Existing benchmark curves and runtime values remain unchanged; these are new results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The Bellman bounds, reward conditions, additivity lemma, complexity expressions, and telescoping proof remain unchanged. The standard hypervolume formula and clarified vector and optimization notation explain the existing mathematics rather than introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and summary retain the same novelty claims, three acquisition-function contributions, and claims of improved optimization under limited budgets. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning long-horizon uncertainty, computational trade-offs, and information-gain monotonicity are retained. The limitations concerning lower-bound tightness and the adaptivity gap also remain. The scalarization qualifications are relocated, not newly introduced.

D1.justification: The code link, BoTorch implementation information, GP kernel, GPU specification, runtime measurement details, and reduction of JESMO Pareto samples from ten to four already appear in v1. Apart from identifying the added DTLZ configurations, v2 supplies no new implementation or access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 3 expands citations and discussion of non-myopic planning and active search, engineering applications, and combinatorial-space BO. Examples include Jiang et al. (2017) and Kharkovskii et al. (2020). The central positioning as the first finite-horizon non-myopic MOBO framework remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include an explicit hypervolume explanation, clearer acquisition-function notation, wording corrections, acknowledgments, and relocation of alternative-scalarization discussion into Appendix A.3.

P2.justification: The document adopts TMLR formatting throughout, changing typography, spacing, headings, author layout, running headers, and figure/table placement. A new four-panel DTLZ figure is added. Existing plots are largely reused or resized, while the additional-baseline figure and the two tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The DTLZ experiments provide useful new evidence for four- and five-objective optimization, while clearer hypervolume and algorithm notation improve readability. The original methods, proof, and results remain intact. The gain is limited by the brief analysis of the new experiments and the omission of their reference points from the benchmark-details table.
